AttachmentMeta.description: One attachment of the message as the signer describes it: the hash of the file name, the hash of the decoded bytes, their size, and the declared media type.

filename.description: The hash of the attachment's file NAME, not the name: 64 lowercase hex digits of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the name after trimming, with the fallback `unnamed` for an empty name, and lower-cased by the client. An optional `sha256:` prefix is accepted. A file name is content about the message (see `../spec/signature-input.md` §7 in this package), so a value that is not 64 lowercase hex digits is refused with 422. A name that is ITSELF 64 lowercase hex digits is the one shape this cannot be told apart from a hash.
filename.title: Filename

hash.description: SHA-256 over the DECODED bytes of the attachment, standard base64: 43 characters of the alphabet and one `=`. Any other shape is refused with 422.
hash.title: Hash

size.description: The size in bytes of those decoded bytes, as the signer counted them. Greater than zero.

note.description: `null` on an ordinary row. `attachment_signature_invalid` and `attachment_identity_not_active` are written on a row that was sent AS an attached message and could not be read as one — the row is kept so the sender finds their forward in the list, but it is recorded as a plain copy and its verdict is the text comparison and not a signature check. A reader that marks a row as verified checks this field: a row of kind `attachment` that carries either value was not verified.

info.description:
The paths a third-party client needs in order to sign a message through a ZEKNOP relay or to check a signature it received, plus the paths the verification portal reaches without a credential. The rest of the relay's surface — administration, billing, tenant configuration, the keys of a mail server, revocation and erasure — is not part of this document and is not part of what this preview describes.

This file is generated from the relay's own schema and filtered to those paths: the shape is the schema's, and every description is the publisher's public text, which the generator sets in place of the server's own wording. It is not edited by hand. `README.md` beside it carries the semantics a schema cannot state, and `API-CHANGELOG.md` what changed for a caller.

Developer Preview: the protocol and the API may change; nothing here is a security guarantee.

No server is listed on purpose: the base URL is the relay you were given.
info.summary: The part of the ZEKNOP relay's HTTP contract a third-party client uses.
info.title: ZEKNOP relay — public API (Developer Preview)

get.description:
200 with a body naming the state of each datastore the relay cannot serve a request without, and 503 when one of them is unreachable, so an orchestrator can act on the status code alone.

It is outside `/v1`, it carries no contract number, and a client must not read a version or a capability out of it: `GET /v1/capabilities` is the answer a signer acts on, and it stays readable when a datastore is down.
get.summary: Whether this relay can serve requests

post.description:
A deployment that onboards by invitation hands out a code out of band; redeeming it answers with the uuid, the API key and the public key. Single use.

A code the relay does not hold, a code already redeemed, and a code past its expiry are answered identically on every attempt: 404 while no attempt budget is spent, 429 on the attempt that spends one. No answer tells a caller which of its guesses was once a real code. 503 means the attempt budget could not be read, so the code was not looked up at all.

get.description:
The question a signer asks before it writes a version into a message. `signs` and `verifies` are the versions of the signature input this build can construct, oldest first; `signature_input_version` is the newest of them; `contract` is the number of this HTTP contract and `relay_id` names the relay that answered.

No credential, no rate limit of its own, and neither datastore is read: what a build can sign is a property of the build and not of the moment.

A relay from before this route answers 404. A client of this contract reads anything other than a 200 whose body is a JSON object with a list of strings in `signs` as **this relay cannot sign that version**, and does not write the version into a message.
get.summary: Which signature-input versions this relay signs and verifies

get.description:
Every forwarded copy the deployment's checking service received for that envelope id inside the listing window, each row with the time it arrived, the verdict it was given, and whether it arrived as a plain forward or as an attached message. Never a hash, never any text of a copy, and never who forwarded it.

The answer also carries the `identity` block — `uuid`, `domain`, `email`, verification level and type, state — whenever this relay holds a signature for that envelope id, INCLUDING when the list of copies is empty. It is the same identity `GET /v1/signature/{envelope_id}` answers, by the same key and with no credential either.

The whole list is answered and not the latest row, so a copy somebody else pushed in is one more row and never a verdict that replaces another. No credential, rate limited per caller address.

`service_misconfigured: true` is a statement about the deployment's own checking service and not about the envelope id in the path: it is the same answer for every id while it lasts, and it carries no row and no identity.

post.description:
Which way the identity is to be proved decides what happens: `dns_txt` and `domain_manual` register a domain and answer with the challenge to publish, after which `POST /v1/register/verify-domain` activates the identity; the ways that rest on an external identity provider carry that provider's token.

A deployment may not offer every way: one it does not implement is refused with 501. Three codes this route answers are not declared below — 403 when the deployment keeps registration to invited callers and this caller is not one, 409 when that domain is already registered on this relay, and 503 when the store the attempt budgets live in could not be read, in which case nothing was registered and the request may be retried.

A link is sent to the address. The answer carries a polling token and a request code, and no credentials: the page behind the link asks for that code, and an API key exists only once the link has been confirmed with it.

The answer is the same for every address the deployment lets through — in status, in body and in time — whether or not the address already has a registration or a request in progress, because the handler does the same work for every such address (the two rate limits, one polling session, one request code, one queued task) and leaves the lookup, the pending registration, the link and the mail to a task that runs after the answer has been sent. The publisher measures the half about time against a running relay whose mail server holds every conversation open; that test is not part of this package. An address that is already registered gets no mail.

get.description: Polled with the token from `POST /v1/register/mailbox`. `pending` until the link of that request is confirmed with its request code, then `verified` with the uuid, the API key and the public key — once. Afterwards, and after the token expires, 404.
get.summary: Collect the credentials of a confirmed mailbox registration

post.description: Asked after a domain registration. The relay looks for a DNS TXT record at `_zeknop.<domain>` whose value is `zeknop-verify=<uuid>`, and for the file `/.well-known/zeknop-verify.txt` on `https://<domain>` containing the uuid. Either is enough; the answer says which method was found and what the identity state is afterwards.
post.summary: Check a domain challenge and activate the identity

post.description:
The body is `{"token", "code"}` as JSON, or the form of the page above.

The code is compared in constant time. An entry that is not of the code's shape is refused without counting against the link; every well-formed wrong entry counts, and after a fixed number of them the link is withdrawn. With the right code the link is spent, the identity becomes active in one transaction that also removes the other pending registrations of that address, and the credentials are left for the polling session of THAT registration only — this answer itself carries no credentials.
post.summary: Confirm a mailbox link with its request code

get.description: Opened from the mail. It changes nothing — mail scanners follow links — and asks for the request code that the client which started the registration showed; its form posts to `POST /v1/register/verify-mailbox/confirm`. A client that asks for JSON is told the same thing in JSON.
get.summary: The page the magic link opens

post.description:
The signer sends the identity, the hashes of the message it is about to send, the time, and the version and algorithm it signs under; the answer carries the signature, the envelope id that goes into the visible envelope, the relay and the moment it signed, and the version and algorithm the signature was made under.

Authenticated with the identity's API key in `X-API-Key`. The timestamp must be within 30 seconds of the relay's clock. The relay builds the signed bytes itself from the version and the algorithm it was given — it never signs bytes a caller handed it.

The optional header `Idempotency-Key` (64 lowercase hex characters) names the request: a repeat under the same name and the same identity, inside the deployment's idempotency window (24 hours by default), is answered with the same signature and the same envelope id, and nothing is signed a second time. A malformed value is refused with 400 rather than ignored.

Beyond the codes declared below this route also answers **403** — the key is good and the relay will still not sign: the identity is not active, or the `From` address is not one that identity may send as, or the deployment's own policy does not let it sign. The README beside this file lists every such undeclared code.
post.summary: Sign the hashes of a message for a registered identity

get.description:
The envelope id is printed in the visible envelope of every signed message, so anyone holding a forwarded copy — or a photograph of one — can ask this. The answer is the identity that signed and the moment it was signed: its `uuid`, its `domain` and its `email`, which for a mailbox identity is the registered address. That is the design and not an oversight — choose which identity you sign with knowing that whoever holds a copy can read it.

It carries no hash, no signature and no attachment metadata: each of those would confirm a guess about what the message said, and the public keys are published beside them.

The id is exactly 8 alphanumeric characters; anything else is 400. No credential, and the route is rate limited per caller address.

post.description:
The verification question: an identity, a signature, the hashes of the message and the version and algorithm the message announces. No credential.

`valid: true` says the signature holds and the identity is active. Every `valid: false` answer carries `reason`, one word for WHICH kind of no it is, and `signature-mismatch` is the only one that is a statement about the message. A request that names no `version` is read as a question about a message from before version 1.4 of the signature input.

Beyond the codes declared below this route also answers **409** — a caller older than the signature it asks about, refused rather than told the message is invalid — and **503** when the store the replay mark lives in cannot be read.

The README beside this file says what the relay does with a repeated question, which answers a caller may deliver on, which it must treat as an outage, and which codes every path answers without declaring them here.
post.summary: Verify a signature against the hashes of a message

get.description:
The registration state of one identity and every public key it has had, each with its algorithm and the window it was valid in, so a message older than the last key re-issue can be checked by someone who does not want to take this relay's word for it. No credential; 404 for an identity this relay has no record of, and — not declared below — 400 when the path carries something that is not a uuid at all.

It checks no signature, so `valid` here says only that the identity is active and `reason` is never set. `POST /v1/verify` is the route that checks one.
